32 The electric current in a wire may be calculated using the equation I = Anvq.
Which statement is not correct?
A
n is the number of charge carriers per unit volume of the wire.
B
nA is the number of charge carriers per unit length of the wire.
C
q is the charge of each charge carrier.
D
v is the velocity of each charge carrier.

hints: Look at the units hidden in $I = Anvq$: $n$ multiplies area $A$ and a length $v \times t$ to count how many carriers pass in time $t$.
Recall that charge carriers in a metal move randomly at high thermal speed with only a very small average drift of order $10^{-4} \text{ m s}^{-1}$ along the wire.
Check which statement claims $v$ describes every individual carrier rather than that small average drift along the current direction.
walkthrough: Identify the model: current is charge passing per unit time. In time $t$, carriers drift distance $vt$, so volume swept is $Avt$.
Count the charge: number of carriers in that volume is $nAvt$, and total charge is $nAvtq$, so $I = nAvtq/t = Anvq$.
This confirms $n$ is number per unit volume, $q$ is charge per carrier, and $nA$ is number in a unit length because volume of a $1 \text{ m}$ length is $A \times 1$.
For $v$, individual electrons have fast random motion in all directions plus a slow average motion along the wire. Only the average contributes to $I$.
Therefore the statement that $v$ is the velocity of each charge carrier is not correct. This is option D.

A.explanation: This is correct physics. $n$ is the number density of carriers with unit $\text{m}^{-3}$, so it is per unit volume.

B.explanation: This is correct physics. Multiplying $n$ by area $A$ gives carriers in a $1 \text{ m}$ slice, so $nA$ is per unit length.

C.explanation: This is correct physics. In $I = Anvq$, $q$ is the charge carried by one carrier, such as $1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ for an electron.

D.explanation: This is not correct. $v$ is the mean drift velocity along the wire, not the actual velocity of each carrier which includes large random thermal motion.
